# A focused grid header button scrolls the header away from its body

## Context

Outside feedback on the 13.3.0 issues showcase reported that "with a filter visibly set, all values were still shown". The reporter could not reproduce it (defect-note `4aa7bdd6` by @neo-opus-grace, next to #19952–#19954). While reproducing it, I found a recipe that leaves every center header label over the wrong column. Under "Type" a reader sees the Summary text, and under "Area" the Type chips, so a filtered column reads as unfiltered. That makes it a candidate explanation for the report, not one confirmed with the reporter.

## The Problem

Reproduced on https://neomjs.com/dist/production/examples/grid/issues/index.html (13.3.0, Chromium, an 800×600 viewport so the center region overflows):

1. Click into "Search records".
2. Press Tab until the Area header button has focus, then Tab once more. Focus moves to its menu button ("Filter Area").
3. The center header row shifts left; the body does not.

Measured: the center `.neo-grid-header-toolbar` has `scrollLeft` 289, while `.neo-grid-horizontal-scrollbar`, which places the body, stays at 0. An automated click that scrolled the Type menu button into view produced the same split (about 140 px). Whether a later body scroll re-aligns them is untested.

## The Architectural Reality

- The horizontal position has one source, the grid's horizontal scrollbar. The main-thread `GridHorizontalScrollSync` copies the scrollbar's `scrollLeft` onto the center header toolbar, and `ScrollManager#onContainerScroll` mirrors it into `headerToolbar.scrollLeft` for the SortZone's math.
- Nothing flows the other way. The center header toolbar is an overflow container, so when focus lands on a header element outside the center clip, the browser scrolls that toolbar by itself. The scrollbar and the body stay where they were.
- **Design authority:** `src/grid/HorizontalScrollbar.mjs` (`endWidth_`) — "`Neo.main.addon.GridHorizontalScrollSync` copies this element's `scrollLeft` verbatim onto the center header toolbar — that 1:1 mapping is only exact when scrollport equals the center clip width." A header toolbar that scrolls on its own breaks that 1:1 mapping.
- `src/grid/header/plugin/Menu.mjs` calls `this.owner.focus()` when its menu closes, so a header whose button sits outside the clip may trigger the same native scroll. This is a hypothesis; I haven't tested it.

## The Fix

Keep the scrollbar the single source. When the center header toolbar scrolls natively, move the horizontal scrollbar to the same position, so the header and body move together and the focused column comes into view. That is what a keyboard user needs. It belongs in the main-thread `GridHorizontalScrollSync`, beside the existing copy. Equal values must not echo back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Focusing a header, or its menu button, outside the center clip leaves the header and body aligned: the center header toolbar's `scrollLeft` equals the horizontal scrollbar's.
- [ ] AC-2: The focused header is visible after the move.
- [ ] AC-3: A browser e2e on the issues showcase at 800×600 is red on base (`scrollLeft` mismatch after tabbing to the Area menu button) and green at head.

## Out of Scope

- A column's own value menu listing every value of that column. That is by design (the counts follow the other filters), and it is the other reading of the report; it is recorded on the defect-note.
- #19952, #19953 and #19954.
